chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who loves that he be upon my fitrah (natural disposition), let him follow my Sunnah, and indeed, marriage is from my Sunnah.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet say about marriage in relation to his Sunnah?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the Prophetic preference for marriage as a rejection of Christian monasticism (Rahbaniyyah), affirming it as a fundamental aspect of the Prophet's Sunnah and natural disposition (fitrah). In Shia scholarship, this is often cited to validate the permissibility and virtue of marital relations, contrasting them with ascetic withdrawal from worldly life. It serves as a juridical basis for viewing marriage not merely as a contract but as an act of worship that completes half of one's faith.
